message.content: {"winner":"B","evidence_A":"About 70 words, within target. Mischaracterizes the article in two ways: it adds \"информационной войны,\" which the source never mentions, and it says media education should be mandatory in higher education, whereas the source calls it optional there. Coverage is decent: manipulation, fake-news examples, falling trust, vertical structure, PR campaign and foreign experience.","evidence_B":"About 85 words, near the upper limit of the length target. Faithful on definitions, disinformation examples, school integration, the ministry-based vertical and Finland's motto. Minor flaws: \"Авторы\" is plural for a single author, the hyphen in \"учебно-методическую\" is missing, and declining trust in media is omitted.","comparative_reason":"A has two substantive fidelity errors: an invented \"information war\" framing and a distortion of the optional status of higher-education media training. B's issues are minor and it adds the concrete Finnish example. On balance, B is more accurate."}
